Information about people who have interacted with Centrelink, including demographics, eligibility for Centrelink benefits, and actual benefits received.

*Defines DOMINO, its longitudinal social-security coverage and official metadata catalogue.*

DSS defines the column as \"The date on which a concession card is actioned, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD\", which makes it a processing date rather than an entitlement date: CARD_ISSUE_DATE is when the card was produced and CARD_START_DATE is when it could first be used. All four concession card tables carry it, so a card's administrative sequence of action, issue, start and expiry reads the same way for a health care card, a pensioner card, a low income card and a seniors health card.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA), column action_date","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/71620","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Concession card action date","k":"Date (YYYY-MM-DD)","def":"A calendar date written YYYY-MM-DD. The domain is open: any date on which Centrelink actioned a card record, which in DOMINO runs from 2000 to the extract date.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA), column action_date","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/71620","lim":"It does not say what the action was. A grant, a reissue after loss, a variation and a cancellation all stamp this one field, so REASON_CODE and END_REASON_CODE are needed to tell them apart. An action date can also fall either side of the card's own start date, so it cannot stand in for the date entitlement began.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / ccd_hcc","madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / ccd_pcc","madipge-dom-monthly-d-families-children / ccd_hcc_lic","madipge-dom-monthly-d-retirement-widows / ccd_shc"]},{"n":"ACTV_PRTCPN_CODE","d":"A flag on a medical or capacity assessment record for whether activity participation requirements applied to the recipient.","full":"A flag on a medical or capacity assessment record for whether activity participation requirements applied to the recipient. DSS defines the element as \"Indicator of activity participant requirements for a medical assessment\", which places it on the assessment rather than on the payment. It sits in the medical conditions detail table with the impairment code and rating, the assessed work capacity and the incapacity period dates, so it qualifies how the assessment was conducted rather than what the person was entitled to.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Activity participant, Code\" (item 54207)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54207","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Activity participation code","k":"domino_activity_participant_code","def":"Three permissible codes — Y for yes, N for no and NR for not required — with a blank as the supplementary missing value. The domain is the DSS permissible value list for the element and carries no other codes.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Activity participant, Code\" (item 54207), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54207","lim":"It records whether requirements applied, not what the person did. The code says nothing about whether an activity was undertaken, attended, exempted or breached, and it carries neither the hours nor the type of activity. Nor does an NR mean the recipient was excused from mutual obligations generally; it means participation requirements were not relevant to this particular assessment.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-disability-carers / mcd_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / mcd_dtls"],"dom":0},{"n":"ADDR_PRTY","d":"Which of a recipient's concurrently held addresses should be treated as their location on a given day.","full":"Which of a recipient's concurrently held addresses should be treated as their location on a given day. DSS defines it as a \"Derived code highlighting address priority for identifying the location of a recipient on a given day\", so it is a tie-breaking rule rather than an observation. On the derived location table it explains why one address episode survived into the geography columns beside it — ARID_HASH_TRUNC, the meshblock and the 2021 ASGS areas — when the person had several addresses recorded at once.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Address: Address priority, Code\" (item 54356)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54356","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Address priority","k":"domino_address_priority_code","def":"A single digit ranking the address types: 1 temporary, 2 term, 3 home, 5 postal or other. The published list has no value 4, and lower numbers take precedence when several address records overlap in time.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Address: Address priority, Code\" (item 54356), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54356","lim":"It is a rule for choosing between addresses, not evidence about any one of them. A row carrying priority 3 does not mean the person had no term or postal address, only that the home address won on that day, and the priority says nothing about how long the address was held or how reliable it is — START_DATE and END_DATE carry the duration.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / loc_derived","madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / loc_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-loc-pos-temp-term-dtls / loc_pos_temp_term_dtls"],"dom":1},{"n":"ADDR_TYPE_CODE","d":"What kind of address the recipient supplied on this address detail record — home, postal, temporary, term, business or a nominee's.","full":"What kind of address the recipient supplied on this address detail record — home, postal, temporary, term, business or a nominee's. DSS defines the element as \"The type of address given by a recipient\". In the address detail table it qualifies POSTCODE, STATE, MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE on the same row, so it decides whether that geography describes where the person lives or only where their mail arrives.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Address: Address type, Code\" (item 369)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/369","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Address type code","k":"domino_address_type_code","def":"Eight three-letter codes: BUS business, FPO FAO postal, HOM home, NAD nominee, PHY physical, POS postal, TEM temporary and TER term address. The list is the DSS permissible value set for the element.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Address: Address type, Code\" (item 369), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/369","lim":"A home address type is not proof of residence at the coded meshblock. Nominee and FAO postal addresses belong to a person acting for the recipient, and a business or postal address can be a workplace or a post office, so residential analysis has to filter to HOM or PHY first. MESHMATCH on the same row separately records whether the meshblock came from the address text or from coordinates.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / loc_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-loc-pos-temp-term-dtls / loc_pos_temp_term_dtls"],"dom":2},{"n":"ADR_TYP","d":"The address type carried on the derived location history, the table that gives a recipient one chosen address per period.","full":"The address type carried on the derived location history, the table that gives a recipient one chosen address per period. DSS defines the underlying element as \"The type of address given by a recipient\". Unlike ADDR_TYPE_CODE in the address detail table, this column describes the address DSS selected for the episode, so it sits with START_DATE, END_DATE, ARID_HASH_TRUNC and the 2021 ASGS geography; POSTALTYPE beside it splits postal addresses further.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Address: Address type, Code\" (item 369), bound to the DOMINO derived location table","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/369","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Type of address (e.g. residential postal etc.)","k":"domino_address_type_code","def":"The same DSS address type domain as ADDR_TYPE_CODE, whose three-letter codes include HOM, POS, TEM and TER, although the PLIDA item list publishes no value list against this particular column.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Address: Address type, Code\" (item 369), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/369","lim":"It is not a second, independent observation of the address type. The derived table keeps one address per date range after ADDR_PRTY has been applied, so a type that lost the priority contest never appears here at all. Counting address types in the derived table therefore under-counts the addresses a person actually held, and a person can look like they never had a postal address when they always did.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / loc_derived"]},{"n":"AGE","d":"A recipient's age in completed years, fixed at a reference date rather than measured at the event on the row.","full":"A recipient's age in completed years, fixed at a reference date rather than measured at the event on the row. Which reference date depends on the table: STATIC_DEMOGS gives \"The age of a person as of the extract date\", while Snap-DOMINO gives \"The age of a person as of the snap date\", the day carried in SNAP_DATE. Age at a payment, a card or an assessment therefore has to be worked out from YEAR_OF_BIRTH and MONTH_OF_BIRTH against that event's own dates.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, distributions SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA, item 110613) and STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA, item 84485)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/110613","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Recipient age as of extract date","k":"Age in completed years","def":"Whole years, format N{NN} on the snapshot distribution, so a two- or three-digit integer with no fractional part and no code list.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, distributions SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA, item 110613) and STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA, item 84485)","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/110613","lim":"It is not age at the event. Joining STATIC_DEMOGS to a payment history record and reading AGE gives the person's age at extraction, which can be many years after the payment, so an 'age at first payment' built this way is wrong by the length of the person's history. The two tables also disagree with each other by design, since one is anchored to the extract and the other to the snapshot day.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / snap_domino_beta","madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / static_demogs"]},{"n":"AGE_GROUP","d":"The recipient's age band on the Snap-DOMINO snapshot date, given as a band rather than a number of years.","full":"The recipient's age band on the Snap-DOMINO snapshot date, given as a band rather than a number of years. DSS defines the element as \"A code set representing chronological groupings of age of a person\". It sits on the point-in-time snapshot table beside AGE, the concession card flags and SNAP_DATE, so it answers what the age profile of the payment population looked like on a chosen day rather than at any event.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Person: Age group\" (item 109634)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/109634","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"A code set representing chronological groupings of age of a person.","k":"domino_snap_age_group","def":"Text band labels rather than numeric codes: Under 16, then 21 to 24, 25 to 34, 35 to 44, 45 to 54, 55 to 64 and 65 and over, with Unknown as a supplementary value. The bands are the DSS permissible values for the element.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Person: Age group\" (item 109634), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column; the published band list runs Under 16 then 21 to 24 upward, with no 16-20 band shown on the page","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/109634","lim":"The published list has a hole in it. No band covers ages 16 to 20, so a count by AGE_GROUP will not sum to the snapshot population and the missing young people are not in Unknown either; use AGE on the same table where a full distribution is needed. The bands are also unequal in width, so a rate calculated per band is not comparable between bands without standardising.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / snap_domino_beta"],"dom":3},{"n":"AMR","d":"The Centrelink work item that created or changed this medical conditions record.","full":"The Centrelink work item that created or changed this medical conditions record. DSS defines it as a \"Unique number/code allocated by Integrated Activity Management (IAM) within the context of a client record\", and its role is as an audit trail: it ties a row back to the activity that produced it, and marks updates that are still provisional or logically deleted. On mcd_dtls it sits beside ASSMT_ID, so AMR answers which piece of Centrelink processing wrote the row while ASSMT_ID answers which medical assessment the condition came from.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 614 'Recipient: Activity Management Reference (AMR) number, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/614","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Activity management reference","k":"Centrelink Integrated Activity Management reference number","def":"A number of up to four digits, format N[4], allocated within one client's record rather than across the population.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 614 'Recipient: Activity Management Reference (AMR) number, Code'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/614","lim":"It is not a person key and not a national identifier, so the same value recurs in unrelated recipients' records and counting distinct values across the file counts nothing. It also carries no date, so it cannot be used to order events within a person's history.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-disability-carers / mcd_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / mcd_dtls"]},{"n":"APT_END_DATE","d":"The day the apprenticeship or traineeship recorded on this row stopped, as DSS puts it the \"End date of an apprentice or traineeship event\".","full":"The day the apprenticeship or traineeship recorded on this row stopped, as DSS puts it the \"End date of an apprentice or traineeship event\". The table carries three dates that do different jobs: APT_START_DATE and this column bound the event as it actually ran, while APT_STDNT_END_DATE is the end that was expected when it started. Comparing the actual end against the expected end is what identifies an early exit, and EUEA_ID groups the rows belonging to one education episode.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, distribution EDU_APPR_TRN_EXT (PLIDA), column apt_end_date","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/71624","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Apprenticeship end date","k":"Date (YYYY-MM-DD)","def":"A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, open domain, empty while the apprenticeship is still running.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, distribution EDU_APPR_TRN_EXT (PLIDA), column apt_end_date","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/71624","lim":"An end date is not evidence of completion. Cancellation, suspension and a transfer to a different employer all close an event, and this table carries no completion flag, so a filled end date on its own cannot separate an apprentice who finished from one who withdrew.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-older-students / edu_appr_trn"]},{"n":"APT_START_DATE","d":"The day the apprenticeship or traineeship on this row began, given by DSS as the \"Start date of an apprentice or traineeship event\".","full":"The day the apprenticeship or traineeship on this row began, given by DSS as the \"Start date of an apprentice or traineeship event\". Only training that touched a Centrelink payment is here, because the table exists to support student and youth payment assessment, so this is not a start date for apprentices in general and cannot be read as a national commencements series. It is also not comparable with the Census language variable, which uses the ABS classification.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / snap_domino_beta","madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / static_demogs"],"dom":27},{"n":"LAST_ACTIVE_ISP","d":"The income support payment the person was on at the close of the active payment spell that the snapshot falls in.","full":"The income support payment the person was on at the close of the active payment spell that the snapshot falls in. With FIRST_ACTIVE_ISP it brackets the spell, so a row shows where a period on income support started and where it finished without joining to the payment history tables. ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE give the dates of that spell, which DOMINO builds by stitching over breaks of up to six weeks.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108856, 'Payment: Last Active ISP'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108856","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Last payment in active Income Support Payment period","k":"DSS benefit type code","def":"A three or four character code from the DSS benefit type code set, which the registry defines as \"A code set representing government benefits\" and which runs to about a hundred values: AGE for Age Pension, JSP for JobSeeker Payment, DSP for Disability Support Pension, PPS for Parenting Payment Single.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108856, 'Payment: Last Active ISP'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108856","lim":"It names the last payment inside one stitched spell, not the last payment a person ever received, so a person who returns to income support after a longer break starts a new spell with its own closing payment. The column also gives no date for the change and no reason for it.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / snap_domino_beta"]},{"n":"LGA","d":"The council area the person's address fell in on the snapshot date.","full":"The council area the person's address fell in on the snapshot date. The DSS registry defines it as \"The designated region representing the whole geographical area of responsibility of an incorporated Local Government entity in which a given address is located, as represented by a code\", which makes it the one geography on the snapshot table that matches an actual unit of government rather than a statistical area. It is the natural join for council-level service planning, while SA2, SA3 and SA4 on the same row are the ABS statistical alternatives.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108688, 'Address: Local Government Area (ASGS 2021), Code NNNNN'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108688","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Local government area","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS Local Government Area code (2021)","def":"A code of up to five characters from the Local Government Areas (LGA) Code (2021) value domain, the ASGS code set for the council area a location belongs to.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108688, 'Address: Local Government Area (ASGS 2021), Code NNNNN'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108688","lim":"LGAs do not nest inside the SA3 or SA4 codes beside them, and not every value is a council: where no incorporated local government exists the ABS codes the area as Unincorporated followed by the state or territory, which covers the whole of the Australian Capital Territory, northern South Australia and some other territories. Council amalgamations also retire and mint codes, so an LGA time series breaks where boundaries were redrawn.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / snap_domino_beta"],"dom":28},{"n":"LVL_ATTAINED","d":"The highest completed level of education Centrelink holds for the person.","full":"The highest completed level of education Centrelink holds for the person. DSS says the element \"Refers to completed education, not a current course of study being undertaken by a recipient\" and that \"The most recent level of educational attainment is recorded\", which makes edu_lvl the attainment table and edu_ftb and edu_dtls the enrolment tables. STDNT_STS_CODE on the same row gives the person's study status when the attainment was recorded.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Level of educational attainment, Code\" (item 703)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/703","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Education level attained code","k":"domino_educational_attainment_code","def":"A three-character code, format XXX, from a 28-value DSS attainment list. It runs U10 less than Year 10 and Y10 to Y13, certificates C01 to C04, then ASD, DIP, ADP, BAC, HNR, MST, PGR and DOC, with TRA trade qualification, HEB bridging course, UGR undergraduate, UNK unknown, and several entries marked no longer valid.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Level of educational attainment, Code\" (item 703), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/703","lim":"It is neither ASCED nor the Census attainment items, so it will not concord to ABS education counts without a mapping. Attainment is recorded when Centrelink has a reason to ask, so it is absent for people never assessed for a study-related payment and can be years out of date for people who qualified after their last assessment.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / edu_lvl"],"dom":29},{"n":"LVL_ATTAINED_DESC","d":"The text form of the attainment level held as a code in LVL_ATTAINED on the same row.","full":"The text form of the attainment level held as a code in LVL_ATTAINED on the same row. DSS defines the element as \"The level of educational attainment of a recipient represented as text\", so the two columns express one value domain, one as a code and one as its label. Carrying both is a convenience of the extract rather than two separate facts about the person.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Level of educational attainment, Text\" (item 51677)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/51677","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Education level attained description","k":"domino_educational_attainment_text","def":"A string carrying the label of the attainment level, such as Bachelor's Degree, Certificate 3, Year 12 or Trade Qualification. The set matches the 28 labels behind LVL_ATTAINED, including those marked no longer valid, with a no-value label where attainment is not recorded.","p":"2000 to current","s":"guessed","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Level of educational attainment, Text\" (item 51677), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column; the element is the text representation of the same value domain (item 83) used by LVL_ATTAINED","lim":"Being a label rather than a code, joins and grouping are exposed to punctuation and casing, so Bachelor's Degree with an apostrophe will not match Bachelors Degree. Prefer LVL_ATTAINED for any tabulation, and treat this column as display text.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / edu_lvl"],"dom":30},{"n":"MAN_CODE","d":"The ground on which Disability Support Pension was granted without a full impairment assessment.","full":"The ground on which Disability Support Pension was granted without a full impairment assessment. DSS defines the element as \"A code describing the manifest disability of the recipient\", covering manifest grants such as permanent blindness, terminal illness or a nursing home level of care. Its presence on a record explains why IMPRMT_CODE and the medical condition groups can be sparse on the same assessment.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Manifestly disabled, Code\" (item 629)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/629","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Manifestly disabled code","k":"domino_manifestly_disabled_code","def":"A three-character code, format XXX, from a 14-value list. It names the manifest ground (BLI permanent blindness, TRM terminal illness, INT intellectual disability, HV4 category 4 HIV or AIDS, NHM nursing home level of care, TPI special rate or Military Rehabilitation Act) and the outcomes MCW, MDI, MNI, MWK and MWL that record a manifest claim not accepted.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Manifestly disabled, Code\" (item 629), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/629","lim":"It is a claim-processing pathway, not a diagnosis or a severity ranking, so a person with a serious condition assessed the usual way carries nothing here. Several codes record an unsuccessful manifest test while reading like conditions, so treating every non-blank value as a manifest grant overstates the count.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-disability-carers / mcd_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / mcd_dtls"],"dom":31},{"n":"MB_ASGS_2021","d":"The mesh block the person's address fell in, on the derived location table that holds one row per address episode.","full":"The mesh block the person's address fell in, on the derived location table that holds one row per address episode. The DSS registry defines mesh blocks as \"the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS\" that \"form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)\", so this is the finest geography DOMINO publishes and everything else on the row aggregates from it. SA1_ASGS_2021, SA2_ASGS_2021, SA4_ASGS_2021 and STATE_ASGS_2021 are the same address at coarser levels, ARID_HASH_TRUNC identifies the address itself, and START_DATE and END_DATE bound the period the person was there.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108891, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 Meshblock, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108891","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Mesh block coded to 2021 asgs","k":"ASGS 2021 Mesh Block code","def":"An eleven-digit ASGS 2021 mesh block code, format N(11), whose leading digit is the state or territory. Mesh blocks nest exactly inside SA1s, so the SA1 column on the same row is a strict aggregation of this one.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108891, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 Meshblock, Code'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108891","lim":"The ABS designs a mesh block to hold roughly 30 to 60 dwellings, so it is a small area, not a dwelling or a household: two people sharing a code are neighbours and need not live together. Boundaries were redrawn between ASGS editions, so a 2021 code cannot be compared with the differently coded MESHBLOCK column in loc_dtls without a correspondence file.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / loc_derived"]},{"n":"MED_PRMY_GRP","d":"The broad group of the main medical condition recorded at a Disability Support Pension medical assessment.","full":"The broad group of the main medical condition recorded at a Disability Support Pension medical assessment. DSS defines the element as \"A recipient's primary medical condition, as represented by a code\" and notes it is a high level grouping produced through a concordance rather than a code the assessor typed. MED_SCNDRY_GRP holds the same grouping for a second condition, and IMPRMT_CODE holds the rating attached to the assessment.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Primary medical condition group, Code\" (item 107942)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/107942","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Primary medical code","k":"domino_medical_condition_group_code","def":"A three-letter code, format AAA, from a 23-value condition group list. Groups follow body systems and impairment types, including MUS musculo-skeletal and connective tissue, PSY psychological or psychiatric, CIR circulatory, NER nervous system, INT intellectual or learning and CAN cancer or tumour, with PFC poorly defined cause and UNK for grants made before 12 November 1991.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Primary medical condition group, Code\" (item 107942), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/107942","lim":"It is an aggregation, not a diagnosis: no ICD code sits behind it in the extract, so conditions within a group cannot be separated. Records exist only where a medical assessment took place, so the column describes assessed claimants rather than disability across the DOMINO population.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-disability-carers / mcd_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / mcd_dtls"],"dom":11},{"n":"MED_SCNDRY_GRP","d":"The condition group for a second medical condition recorded at the same assessment as MED_PRMY_GRP.","full":"The condition group for a second medical condition recorded at the same assessment as MED_PRMY_GRP. DSS defines it as \"A recipient's secondary medical condition represented at a higher level of aggregation\" using the primary condition's groups, so the two columns are directly comparable. MED_SCNDRY_ID and MED_SCNDRY_PERM beside it identify the secondary condition record and mark whether it is permanent.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Secondary medical condition group, Code\" (item 107944)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/107944","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Secondary medical code","k":"domino_medical_condition_group_code","def":"A three-letter code, format AAA, sharing the 23-value medical condition group domain used by MED_PRMY_GRP, so the same group codes appear with the same meanings on both columns.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Secondary medical condition group, Code\" (item 107944), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/107944","lim":"A blank means no secondary condition was recorded at that assessment, which is not evidence of a single condition, and any third or later condition has nowhere to go in this structure. Primary and secondary also reflect the assessment's ordering for payment purposes, not which condition affects the person most.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-disability-carers / mcd_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / mcd_dtls"],"dom":11},{"n":"MED_SCNDRY_ID","d":"Links a secondary medical condition record to the earlier record it replaced, so the condition history reads as a sequence of corrections rather than as a set of separate conditions.","full":"Links a secondary medical condition record to the earlier record it replaced, so the condition history reads as a sequence of corrections rather than as a set of separate conditions. The DSS registry defines it as \"An identifier that links a medical condition that has been overwritten\". It sits on the medical conditions details table beside MED_SCNDRY_GRP, which names the condition group, and MED_SCNDRY_PERM, which records how lasting the condition was judged to be.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 635, 'Recipient: Secondary medical condition identifier, ID number'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/635","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Secondary medical code identifier","k":"Secondary medical condition record identifier","def":"A short number, one or two digits, from the registry's Secondary medical condition ID number domain, which auto-increments from 1. It distinguishes successive versions of a record rather than naming a condition.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 635, 'Recipient: Secondary medical condition identifier, ID number'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/635","lim":"The number carries no clinical meaning and cannot be used to identify or count conditions; MED_SCNDRY_GRP is the column that names what the condition was. Its absence means no record was overwritten, not that the person had no secondary condition, so treating a populated value as evidence of a second diagnosis double counts corrections as conditions.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-disability-carers / mcd_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / mcd_dtls"]},{"n":"MED_SCNDRY_PERM","d":"Records how lasting the medical condition on this row was judged to be, which is the assessment that decides whether a condition can support a Disability Support Pension claim.","full":"Records how lasting the medical condition on this row was judged to be, which is the assessment that decides whether a condition can support a Disability Support Pension claim. The DSS registry binds the column to a data element defined as \"The permanency of a recipient's primary medical condition, as represented by a code\", and its five codes separate a permanent condition that has been diagnosed, treated and stabilised from one that is recurring or temporary. PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE bound the assessment, and IMPRMT_RATE on the same table carries the impairment rating that goes with it.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 230, 'Recipient: Primary medical condition permanency, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/230","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Secondary medical code pemanent indicator","k":"DSS medical condition permanency code","def":"One character from the DSS permanency code set: D for permanent, diagnosed, treated and stabilised; P for permanent, not diagnosed, treated and stabilised; M for permanent; R for recurring; T for temporary.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 230, 'Recipient: Primary medical condition permanency, Code'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/230","lim":"Permanency here is an administrative judgement made for payment purposes, not a clinical prognosis, and a T does not mean a doctor expected recovery. The registry also ties this column to the primary condition data element while the PLIDA data item list calls it secondary, so check it against MED_PRMY_GRP and MED_SCNDRY_GRP before assuming which condition it qualifies.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-disability-carers / mcd_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / mcd_dtls"]},{"n":"MESHBLOCK","d":"The mesh block the address Centrelink held for the person fell in, one row per address period on the location details table.","full":"The mesh block the address Centrelink held for the person fell in, one row per address period on the location details table. The DSS registry defines mesh blocks as \"the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS\" that \"form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)\", so it is the finest location DOMINO records for a person. MESHMATCH beside it says whether the code came from matching the address itself or only its coordinates, SA1_MAINCODE, SA2_MAINCODE, POSTCODE and STATE are the same address at coarser levels, and the column repeats on the temporary and terminated address table and on snap_domino_beta.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108891, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 Meshblock, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108891","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Asgs 2016 meshblock","k":"ASGS Mesh Block code","def":"An eleven-digit mesh block code. The PLIDA data item list labels this column ASGS 2016 while the DSS registry maps it to the ASGS 2021 mesh block data element, so confirm the edition against the extract's reference period before joining to boundary files.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108891, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 Meshblock, Code'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108891","lim":"A mesh block is not a dwelling or a household, so two people with the same code live in the same small area rather than the same home. The code also describes where Centrelink last recorded the person, so it lags an unreported move, and where MESHMATCH is blank the address never matched at all and the geography columns on the row are empty rather than wrong.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / loc_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / snap_domino_beta","madipge-dom-monthly-d-loc-pos-temp-term-dtls / loc_pos_temp_term_dtls"]},{"n":"MESHMATCH","d":"Says how the mesh block on the same row was derived: from the address text, or from the coordinates behind it.","full":"Says how the mesh block on the same row was derived: from the address text, or from the coordinates behind it. The DSS registry defines it as an \"Indicator identifying if a meshblock code was matched by address or longitude/latitude coordinates\", which makes it the quality flag for every geography column on the location details table. It matters because a coordinate match can put a record on the wrong side of a boundary, so MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE are less reliable at fine resolution where this column reads L.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 54357, 'Address: Meshblock matched indicator, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54357","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Meshblock matched (by address or long/lat coordinates) indicator","k":"Meshblock match method code","def":"One character: A where the mesh block was matched by address and L where it was matched by latitude and longitude. A blank is the registry's supplementary value, meaning the address was not matched at all.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 54357, 'Address: Meshblock matched indicator, Code'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54357","lim":"It grades how the geocode was obtained, not whether the address was correct, so a stale or mistyped address that geocodes cleanly still returns A. It also says nothing about whether the person actually lived there, only about the matching step that produced the codes.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / loc_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-loc-pos-temp-term-dtls / loc_pos_temp_term_dtls"]},{"n":"MONTH_OF_BIRTH","d":"The month the person was born, held separately from YEAR_OF_BIRTH because the PLIDA release of DOMINO carries no full date of birth.","full":"The month the person was born, held separately from YEAR_OF_BIRTH because the PLIDA release of DOMINO carries no full date of birth. The department's internal equivalent of this table, stt_pit_ext, holds a single date of birth as YYYY-MM-DD; the PLIDA version splits it into month and year, which is a disclosure control rather than a difference in what was collected. Combined with YEAR_OF_BIRTH it fixes a person's age to within a month, and AGE on the same row gives their age as at the extract date.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry distribution 84485, 'STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA)'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/84485","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Birth month","k":"Calendar month of birth","def":"A calendar month. The DSS registry restricts the metadata for this column, so neither the coding, the width nor the treatment of missing values is published, and the value should be inspected in the extract before use.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry distribution 84485, 'STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA)'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/84485","lim":"There is no day of birth, so an exact age on a given date cannot be calculated and anyone whose birthday falls in the month of an event sits on either side of an age threshold with equal probability. That matters for payments with sharp age tests, such as the move from Youth Allowance to JobSeeker Payment or reaching Age Pension age, where a month of uncertainty is enough to misclassify eligibility.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / static_demogs"]},{"n":"NEXT_ISP","d":"The income support payment the person moves onto next within the same active payment spell.","full":"The income support payment the person moves onto next within the same active payment spell. With PREV_ISP it lets one snapshot row be read as a transition rather than a state: Parenting Payment Single to JobSeeker Payment as a youngest child ages out, or JobSeeker Payment to Disability Support Pension after a successful claim. Where the current payment is the last in the spell there is nothing to point to, and LAST_ACTIVE_ISP names the closing payment instead.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108855, 'Payment: Next Income Support Payment'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108855","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Refers to the next Income Support Payment type benefit (in this period of activity)","k":"DSS benefit type code","def":"A three or four character code from the DSS benefit type code set, which the registry defines as \"A code set representing government benefits\" and which covers about a hundred payments: AGE for Age Pension, JSP for JobSeeker Payment, DSP for Disability Support Pension, CAR for Carer Payment.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108855, 'Payment: Next Income Support Payment'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108855","lim":"The next payment is scoped to the current spell, so a payment taken up after a break too long to be stitched into that spell never appears here. The column also carries no date, so it says a transition happened without saying when, and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE bounds the whole spell rather than the changeover.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / snap_domino_beta"]},{"n":"NSPP_PRCPL_CARER_RSN_CODE","d":"Why the person is not treated as the principal carer of a dependent child.","full":"Why the person is not treated as the principal carer of a dependent child. DSS records the element as one \"used to record Principal Carer reason value\", and every published code is a negative ground, so it explains the absence of the status that PRINCIPAL_PARENT_IND on the same row flags. Principal carer status changes participation requirements and payment rates, which is why the reason is kept at all.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Principal Carer Reason, Code\" (item 54745)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54745","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Principal carer reason code","k":"domino_principal_carer_reason_code","def":"A three-character code, format XXX, with a four-value published list: NDE no dependent children, PCC partner is principal carer, NPC not principal carer, and a blank.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Recipient: Principal Carer Reason, Code\" (item 54745), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54745","lim":"It cannot confirm that someone is a principal carer, since the codes name reasons they are not, so both presence and absence have to be read against PRINCIPAL_PARENT_IND. It also names no child and gives no count, so it does not stand in for the family composition tables.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-families-children / cir_prin_car","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / cir_prin_car"],"dom":32},{"n":"OBJECT_TYPE_CODE","d":"Says what kind of entity the demographic record describes: a person, a child, or an organisation.","full":"Says what kind of entity the demographic record describes: a person, a child, or an organisation. The DSS registry defines the column as containing \"the Object Type code (PER/CHI/ORG) for the Customer\", and it matters because DOMINO's customer records are not all adults with a claim of their own. Children listed on a carer's or a family payment record, and organisations acting as nominees or payees, sit in the same customer table, so this is the column that keeps them out of a count of recipients.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 54775, 'Recipient: Object Type, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54775","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Object type code","k":"DSS object type code","def":"A three-character code with three permissible values: PER, CHI and ORG. The registry publishes the codes without written meanings, so the expansions to person, child and organisation come from the code letters themselves.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 54775, 'Recipient: Object Type, Code'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54775","lim":"It classifies the record, not a person's role in a payment: a CHI record does not say which payment the child was listed against or who claimed for them, and the relationship tables carry that link. Filtering to PER is also not the same as filtering to adults, because the object type follows how the record was created rather than the person's age now.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / static_demogs"]},{"n":"PARTNERED_STATUS","d":"Says whether Centrelink had the person recorded as a member of a couple on the snapshot date.","full":"Says whether Centrelink had the person recorded as a member of a couple on the snapshot date. Partnered status drives rates, income tests and asset tests across almost every payment, so it explains rate differences on the snapshot table that ISP_TYPE_CODE alone cannot. EXT_DOM_HOUSEHOLD_ID pairs the person with their partner by concatenating the two DOMINO person identifiers, so a Y here should sit beside a two-person household identifier.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108240, 'Partnered status'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108240","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"The active partnership status of a person, represented by a flag.","k":"Yes/no/unknown flag","def":"One alphabetic character: Y for partnered and N for not partnered, with U as the registry's supplementary value for unknown. Three states can therefore appear.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108240, 'Partnered status'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108240","lim":"It is a social security assessment of whether a couple relationship exists, not a marital status, so a de facto couple reads as Y and a married couple who have separated under one roof can read as N. It also refers only to the snapshot date and says nothing about how long the relationship had been recorded or how often it changed.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / snap_domino_beta"]},{"n":"PEN_BLIND_START_DATE","d":"The date a person's blindness was diagnosed, which is the qualifying date for the blind rate of Age Pension or Disability Support Pension.","full":"The date a person's blindness was diagnosed, which is the qualifying date for the blind rate of Age Pension or Disability Support Pension. The DSS registry defines it as \"The date upon which a recipient's blindness was diagnosed by an ophthalmologist, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD\". It is the only medical field on the static demographics table, and it belongs there rather than in the dated medical condition records because blind status is assessed once and then attaches to the person.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 615, 'Person: Blindness start date, YYYY-MM-DD'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/615","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Recipient pension blindness start date","k":"Date","def":"A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, ten characters, from the registry's Date YYYY-MM-DD value domain. The ABS designs SA1s, in the registry's words, \"to maximise the geographic detail available for Census of Population and Housing data\", which makes this the level at which a DOMINO record can be joined to Census small-area counts or to SEIFA. MB_ASGS_2021 on the same row is finer, SA2_ASGS_2021 and SA4_ASGS_2021 coarser, ARID_HASH_TRUNC identifies the address itself, and START_DATE and END_DATE bound the period.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108892, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA1 main code, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108892","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sa1 location","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code","def":"An eleven-character ASGS 2021 SA1 code. MESHBLOCK beside it is finer and SA2_MAINCODE coarser, MESHMATCH says whether the code came from the address or only its coordinates, and PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE bound the period the address applied.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108892, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA1 main code, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108892","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Asgs sa1 maincode","k":"ASGS Statistical Area Level 1 main code","def":"An eleven-character SA1 main code. The registry defines SA2s as \"medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s)\" whose purpose is \"to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically\", which makes this the middle rung of the row's geography: MB_ASGS_2021 and SA1_ASGS_2021 are finer, SA4_ASGS_2021 and STATE_ASGS_2021 coarser. Because START_DATE and END_DATE bound the episode, changes in this column over a person's rows are the residential moves DOMINO can see.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108679, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA2 main code, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108679","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sa2 location","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code","def":"An ASGS 2021 SA2 code. SA1_MAINCODE and MESHBLOCK are finer, POSTCODE and STATE are the non-ABS alternatives, and MESHMATCH grades how the codes were derived.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108679, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA2 main code, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108679","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Asgs sa2 maincode","k":"ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 main code","def":"An SA2 main code. SA4 boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively. They are designed with an emphasis on stability over time to support the time series of statistical releases such as the Quarterly Labour Force publication. These areas represent labour markets or groups of labour markets within each state and territory, represented as a code.","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 4 code","def":"An ASGS 2021 SA4 code. MB_ASGS_2021, SA1_ASGS_2021 and SA2_ASGS_2021 are the finer views of the same address.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 108680, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 SA4 main code, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108680","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sa4 location","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 4 code","def":"An ASGS 2021 SA4 code, recorded in the registry with a four-digit format. It sits with SHC_AN_INC_TXB, SHC_AN_INC_FGN, SHC_AN_PRP_LOS, SHC_AN_EMP_BEN and SHC_AN_SAL_SCF, which together make up the adjusted taxable income the card is tested on, and PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE bound the year it covers.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 499, 'Recipient: Annual deemed income, Total Australian currency'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/499","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seniors healthcare card income - annual deemed income","k":"Annual amount in Australian dollars","def":"An amount in Australian dollars to two decimal places, format N[9].NN, covering one year. The column exists because the card is tested on adjusted taxable income rather than taxable income, so the amounts a tax return leaves out are collected separately here alongside SHC_AN_SAL_SCF for salary sacrifice, SHC_AN_INC_FGN for foreign income and SHC_AN_PRP_LOS for net investment and property losses.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry data element 498, 'Recipient: Commonwealth Seniors Healthcare Card annual employer provided benefits income, Total Australian currency'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/498","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seniors healthcare card income - annual employer provided benefits income","k":"Annual amount in Australian dollars","def":"An annual amount in Australian dollars to two decimal places, format N[9].NN. The inc_shc table carries one row per annual reporting period, bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE, for people whose card eligibility was assessed. This column is one of seven income components on the row: deemed income, foreign income, employer provided benefits, net property and investment losses and salary sacrificed income sit beside it and are added to it to reach the adjusted taxable income the card is tested against. Within PLIDA the same key runs across products: MBS, PBS, the tax products, Census and the rest carry SYNTHETIC_AEUID under the same custodian description, Synthetic MADIP Person ID, so a DOMINO row joins to another agency's row on this column directly rather than through a separate mapping file.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA)","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/71620","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Synthetic MADIP Person ID","k":"DSS person identifier for linkage (synthetic)","def":"A numeric identifier assigned for linkage, with no meaning in its digits. The column exists because social security law looks through private structures: where a person controls or benefits from a trust or company, its income is attributed to them and tested like their own. The inc_tac table holds nothing else about the entity, so the row is the person, the period bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE, and this amount.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_tac_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1875","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Trust and company daily income amount","k":"Daily income amount in Australian dollars","def":"A daily dollar rate rather than a period total, held to two decimal places in a format of up to nine digits before the point. The mcd_dtls table is the record of medical conditions and work capacity assessments behind disability and participation decisions, holding the primary and secondary condition codes, an impairment rating, and the assessed hours a person can work. This date and its start-date pair bound the window in which the assessment treats the limitation as temporary rather than continuing.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54229","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Temporary limited capacity end date","k":"Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)","def":"A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, set by an assessment rather than by a payment event.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54229","lim":"The close of a temporary limitation is not recovery and not a payment change: the condition codes and the impairment rating on the same row can be unchanged, and whether anything happened to the person's payment is in the payment history tables, not here. A date in the future is the period the assessment set, not an observed end.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-disability-carers / mcd_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / mcd_dtls"]},{"n":"TEMP_LMT_CAP_START_DATE","d":"The day a period of temporarily limited work capacity opens on a medical assessment, defined by DSS as \"The date on which a period of temporary limited capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment starts, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext).","full":"The day a period of temporarily limited work capacity opens on a medical assessment, defined by DSS as \"The date on which a period of temporary limited capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment starts, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext). It marks when an assessor accepted that a condition limits what the person can do for a bounded time, which is the distinction that separates a temporary exemption from participation requirements from a continuing incapacity. INCAP_START and INCAP_END on the same row hold incapacity periods, and IMPRMT_CODE and IMPRMT_RATE hold the impairment that was rated.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54229","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Temporary limited capacity start date","k":"Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)","def":"A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, recorded against the assessment that set the period.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54229","lim":"It dates a decision, not the onset of a condition: a person can be unwell long before an assessment records a limited capacity, and someone who never had an assessment has no row at all. Reduced capacity is the milder of the two temporary findings on this table: limited capacity suspends what a person can be asked to do, while reduced capacity cuts the hours, and TEMP_REDN_CAP_HRS_NUM holds the size of that cut. Reading the two together shows whether an assessment stopped or merely trimmed a person's participation obligations.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54229","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Temporary reduced capacity end date","k":"Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD)","def":"A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, closing a period set by an assessment.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54229","lim":"No matching start-date column is published for the reduced-capacity period, so its beginning has to be inferred from PERIOD_START_DATE or from the preceding assessment; do not borrow TEMP_LMT_CAP_START_DATE, which belongs to the limited-capacity finding rather than this one.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-disability-carers / mcd_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / mcd_dtls"]},{"n":"TEMP_REDN_CAP_HRS_NUM","d":"How many weekly hours an assessment took off a person's work capacity for a temporary period, defined by DSS as \"The number of reduction in hours a recipient is able to work in a week\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext).","full":"How many weekly hours an assessment took off a person's work capacity for a temporary period, defined by DSS as \"The number of reduction in hours a recipient is able to work in a week\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext). It is a change, not a level: CURR_CAPCTY_NUM on the same row holds the current assessed capacity in hours a week and WITH_INTRVN_NUM holds the capacity with intervention, so this column has to be read against them to say what the person was assessed as able to do. Weekly hours are the currency of these decisions because payment and participation rules turn on hour thresholds rather than on a diagnosis.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54229","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Temporary reduced capacity hours number","k":"Hours per week","def":"A whole number of hours in a week, recorded against the assessment that made the finding.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/54229","lim":"Assessed hours are not worked hours. Nothing here records whether the person had a job, and actual earnings sit in the employment income tables, so the column cannot be used to measure labour supply. Because the value is a reduction, treating it as remaining capacity inverts its meaning.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-disability-carers / mcd_dtls","madipge-dom-monthly-d-working-age / mcd_dtls"]},{"n":"TERM_ILL","d":"Whether the person being cared for has a terminal illness, defined by DSS as an \"Indicator that a caree has a terminal illness\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_caree_ext).","full":"Whether the person being cared for has a terminal illness, defined by DSS as an \"Indicator that a caree has a terminal illness\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_caree_ext). The mcd_caree table is medical information about care receivers, collected because someone claimed Carer Payment or Carer Allowance for them, so every column on the row describes the cared-for person while the person key on the row is the carer. A terminal illness matters administratively because it changes how a carer claim is assessed and how quickly it can be granted.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_caree_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/60577","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Terminal illness indicator","k":"Yes or no indicator","def":"A yes or no indicator recorded against a care receiver's medical record for the period the row covers.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_caree_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/60577","lim":"The flag belongs to the care receiver, not to the person whose identifier is on the row, so reading it as the carer's own health inverts the record. Carer Payment and Carer Allowance claims turn on a medical report about the person being cared for, and this column is what distinguishes the doctor or specialist who completed one report from another. Rows sharing a value came from the same professional, which is the only clinician-level structure DOMINO carries.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_caree_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/60577","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Treating health professional synthetic id","k":"Treating health professional identifier (synthetic)","def":"A synthetic identifier standing for the professional, with no name, provider number or registration detail in it, and no meaning in its digits.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_caree_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/60577","lim":"Because it is not a foreign key, it cannot be joined to any provider file: not to a Medicare provider number in MBS or PBS, and not to a registration record. The ABS data item list glosses the column as the type of apprenticeship, while the DSS element bound to it is the field of education of the course of study, so the two readings differ and the safer treatment is as the trade or field rather than a contract type. APT_START_DATE, APT_END_DATE and EUEA_ID bound and identify the apprenticeship episode.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Course: Education field of study, Code\" (item 725), read against the ABS PLIDA DOMINO data item list","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/725","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Type of apprenticeship","k":"domino_education_field_of_study_code","def":"A three-letter code, format AAA, from the DSS 111-value education field of study list, the same domain COURSE_TYPE uses, with entries such as ACC accounting, APF full time apprenticeship, DRA drafting and BTH beauty therapy.","p":"2000 to current","s":"guessed","src":"DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element \"Course: Education field of study, Code\" (item 725), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column; the DIL gloss \"Type of apprenticeship\" is looser than the registry definition, \"Field of education of course of study undertaken by a recipient\"","lim":"The published binding and the custodian's own gloss disagree, so a value should be checked against real data before it is read as a field of education. The column also records nothing about the apprenticeship's stage, employer or outcome; the date columns bound the episode and no completion flag is carried.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-older-students / edu_appr_trn"]},{"n":"UNE_DLY_INC_CONT_CMP","d":"Compensation counted as income against a person's payment, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous income from compensation received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext).","full":"Compensation counted as income against a person's payment, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous income from compensation received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). The inc_une_cont table splits recurring unearned income into six named sources, one column each, over a period bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE, with BEN_TYPE naming the payment the income was assessed against. Compensation here means periodic payments such as workers compensation or an insurance income stream, which reduce a payment dollar for dollar under the compensation rules rather than through the ordinary income test.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Continuing unearned daily income - compensation income","k":"Daily income amount in Australian dollars","def":"A daily dollar rate, not a period total. A lump sum settlement produces a preclusion period rather than a daily income rate, so a person with a large payout can show nothing in this column while receiving no payment at all, and the column does not say whether the compensation reduced the payment or by how much.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / inc_une_cont"]},{"n":"UNE_DLY_INC_CONT_FIN","d":"Overseas income counted against a person's payment, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous income from foreign sources received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext).","full":"Overseas income counted against a person's payment, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous income from foreign sources received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). The column sits with five other recurring unearned income sources on the same row, so a person's total assessed unearned income is the sum across them for the period.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Continuing unearned daily income - foreign income","k":"Daily income amount in Australian dollars","def":"A daily dollar rate in Australian currency, converted from the paying country's currency, and variably rounded in the external release.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","lim":"It names neither the country nor the scheme, so an agreement pension cannot be told apart from private overseas income or from a foreign annuity. Because the amount is converted, a change between periods can be an exchange rate movement or a scheduled revaluation rather than any change in the person's circumstances, and no exchange rate or revaluation date is carried to tell the two apart.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / inc_une_cont"]},{"n":"UNE_DLY_INC_CONT_MSS","d":"Income from a person's financial investments, given by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous unearned income from Managed Investments, Securites or Savings received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext), which is what the abbreviation in the column name stands for.","full":"Income from a person's financial investments, given by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous unearned income from Managed Investments, Securites or Savings received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext), which is what the abbreviation in the column name stands for. It is the column that carries the return on savings and market investments for people on payments, and for most recipients that return is set by the deeming rules rather than by what the investment actually paid. The other five recurring sources on the row are compensation, foreign income, superannuation, other government payments and a residual bucket.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Continuing unearned daily income - min/siv/sav income","k":"Daily income amount in Australian dollars","def":"A daily dollar rate covering three sources in one figure, variably rounded in the external release.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","lim":"The three sources are not separable: a term deposit, a managed fund and a share parcel produce one number, so the column cannot support any statement about what people invest in. It also holds income, not the value of the assets, which are assessed separately and are not in this table, and it does not say whether the figure was deemed or actual.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / inc_une_cont"]},{"n":"UNE_DLY_INC_CONT_OGP","d":"Money from another government payment counted as income against this person's Centrelink payment, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous income from other government payments received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext).","full":"Money from another government payment counted as income against this person's Centrelink payment, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous income from other government payments received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). Veterans' payments and some state or foreign government support are assessable this way, so a person can hold a Centrelink payment at a reduced rate because of an entitlement paid by someone else. BEN_TYPE on the same row says which Centrelink payment the income was assessed against.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Continuing unearned daily income - other government payment income","k":"Daily income amount in Australian dollars","def":"A daily dollar rate over the row's period, variably rounded in the external release.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","lim":"It records income counted against this person's payment, not the other payment itself, so it is not a source of truth about what any other agency paid. DOMINO holds Department of Veterans' Affairs amounts in its own income table as well, so adding this column to those figures will double count the same money.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / inc_une_cont"]},{"n":"UNE_DLY_INC_CONT_OIN","d":"The residual column for recurring unearned income, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous unearned income from other sources received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext).","full":"The residual column for recurring unearned income, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous unearned income from other sources received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). It takes whatever regular non-work income did not fit the five named sources on the row, which are compensation, foreign income, managed investments and savings, superannuation and other government payments. A value here is the assessed daily rate for that leftover income over the row's period.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Continuing unearned daily income - other income","k":"Daily income amount in Australian dollars","def":"A daily dollar rate over the row's period, variably rounded in the external release.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","lim":"Being a residual, the column has no subject matter of its own: a large amount says only that it was not one of the five named types, so it cannot be interpreted as rent, royalties, maintenance or anything else. Its composition can also change as coding practice changes, which makes it unsafe to compare across years without checking the named columns beside it.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / inc_une_cont"]},{"n":"UNE_DLY_INC_CONT_SUP","d":"Superannuation counted as income against a person's payment, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous income from superannuation received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext).","full":"Superannuation counted as income against a person's payment, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of continuous income from superannuation received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_une_cont_ext). It matters most for people of pension age drawing an income stream while holding a part rate of Age Pension, and it is one of six recurring unearned income sources held side by side for the same period. The row says what was assessed, so the column answers how much of a person's superannuation the means test counted, not what their fund holds.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Continuing unearned daily income - superannuation income","k":"Daily income amount in Australian dollars","def":"A daily dollar rate over the row's period, variably rounded in the external release.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_une_cont_ext","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1876","lim":"The assessed amount is not the amount the fund paid. An account-based pension is generally assessed under the deeming rules on the account balance rather than on the drawdown, so a person taking more than the deemed return shows less here than they received, and someone in accumulation phase with a large balance can show nothing at all.","where":["madipge-dom-monthly-d-base / inc_une_cont"]},{"n":"UNE_DLY_INC_VAR","d":"Unearned income that changes from one reporting period to the next, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of variable unearned income received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, data element Recipient: Variable unearned income).","full":"Unearned income that changes from one reporting period to the next, defined by DSS as the \"Daily rate of variable unearned income received by a recipient\" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, data element Recipient: Variable unearned income). The inc_une_var table is the counterpart to inc_une_cont: the continuing table splits steady income into six named sources, while this one carries the fluctuating amount as a single figure, with BEN_TYPE naming the payment it was assessed against and TASK_CODE saying what prompted the record. It answers how much irregular non-work income was counted against a payment over a period.","dsrc":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, data element Recipient: Variable unearned income, Total Australian currency","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/579","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Variable unearned daily income","k":"Daily income amount in Australian dollars","def":"A daily dollar rate in Australian currency, held to two decimal places in a format of up to nine digits before the point, and variably rounded in the external release.","p":"2000 to current","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Aristotle metadata registry, data element Recipient: Variable unearned income, Total Australian currency","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/579","lim":"The amount is not split by source, so unlike the continuing table it cannot tell you where the income came from.
